newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says will announce tax cuts within days.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says will announce tax cuts within days.

text.p: The Egyptian government will announce income tax cuts within days, Finance Minister Mohieddin el-Gharib said in an interview published on Tuesday.
Gharib also confirmed that this month's cuts in import duties did not apply to imports of cars likely to compete with locally assembled models.

"Income tax will be cut in the coming period because the maximum rate is seen as very high. The cuts will apply to individuals and (private) companies but it will be gradual and conditional on our success in stamping out tax evasion," he told the government newspaper al-Ahram.
"In the coming days we will announce the new measures for reducing income tax," he added.
Egypt taxes individual salaries and profits from private companies at 20 percent for the first 50,000 pounds ($14,700) a year and 32 percent for amounts above that threshold.
Gharib said that the only cars affected by the import duty cuts were large models which are not assembled in Egypt. For these the duty has fallen to 135 percent from 160 percent.
"No state in the world imposes this high level (160 percent) of duty on any type of goods, and naturally this measure will not affect the local industry," he added.
The import duty on small cars which compete with locally asembled models remains at 70 percent.
Car assembly companies have argued that they set up their plants in Egypt on the understanding protection would continue.

Asked about the Middle East economic conference set to take place in Cairo in November, Gharib said it should not be affected by recent Middle East violence, born of Palestinian frustration over a lack of progress in peace talks with Israel.

"And I believe that in the long term the government of Israel will not continue with these policies, which go against the interests of its people. Israeli businessmen oppose these policies, which harm them and their interests," he added.
"Working for peace is what will win in the end," he said.
